subject: Physics
description: Reflection, refraction, lenses, human eye, colour

questions.stem: The SPEED OF LIGHT in vacuum is approximately:
questions.explanation: c = 299,792,458 m/s ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s in vacuum. In water c reduces to ~2.25 × 10⁸ m/s (n = 1.33). In glass ~2 × 10⁸ m/s (n ~1.5). Light TRAVELS SLOWER in denser media.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: A CONVEX lens is also called a:
questions.explanation: Convex — thicker at centre, converges parallel rays to a focal point. Used in magnifying glass, human eye lens, camera lens. CONCAVE lens is diverging (thinner at centre).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The defect of vision in which a person cannot see DISTANT objects clearly is called:
questions.explanation: Myopia — image forms BEFORE the retina; corrected with concave (diverging) lens. Hypermetropia — image forms BEHIND retina; corrected with convex lens. Presbyopia — age-related inability to focus on near objects. Astigmatism — irregular curvature of cornea, corrected with cylindrical lens. short-sightedness.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The phenomenon of splitting of WHITE LIGHT into its component colours (VIBGYOR) by a prism is called:
questions.explanation: Dispersion — different wavelengths of white light refract by different amounts through a prism, producing spectrum VIBGYOR. Violet bends the most, Red the least. Newton's classic experiment.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The RAINBOW is formed due to:

options.option_text: Refraction, internal reflection, and dispersion inside water droplets

questions.explanation: Sunlight refracts as it enters a water droplet, disperses into colours, undergoes total internal reflection at the back of the droplet, and refracts again exiting — producing the rainbow. A secondary (fainter) rainbow forms with two internal reflections; colour order is reversed.
questions.subject: Physics

options.option_text: Molecules of air scatter blue light more than other colours
The ocean reflects onto the atmosphere
Nitrogen molecules are blue in colour

questions.explanation: Rayleigh scattering — scattering intensity ∝ 1/λ⁴ → shorter wavelengths (violet, blue) scatter much more than red/orange. Our eyes are more sensitive to blue than violet, hence blue sky. At sunset, longer path through atmosphere → blue is scattered away before reaching eye, leaving red/orange.
questions.subject: Physics

_fixes.was: Molecules of air scatter blue light more than other colours (Rayleigh scattering)
_fixes.now: Molecules of air scatter blue light more than other colours

questions.stem: The power of a lens is measured in:
questions.explanation: Power (P) = 1 / focal length in metres. Unit: Dioptre (D) = m⁻¹. A +2 D lens has focal length 1/2 = 0.5 m (converging). Negative dioptre = diverging (concave) lens. Spectacle prescriptions use this unit.
